author: Prange, Gordon W.; Goldstein, Donald M.; Dillon, Katherine V.
title: At Dawn We Slept: The Untold Story of Pearl Harbor
notes: Thirty-seven years of research, published after Prange's death by two of his students, and still the fullest narrative of the attack from both sides; it is also the book through which Fuchida's account reached the English-language literature, since Prange interviewed him repeatedly from 1948 onwards and the interviews are the source of the third-wave story. It holds, with source:layton-1985, the position that the fuel and repair installations were the great missed target. **Not read.** The Internet Archive's copies are lending copies; nothing is quoted from it here and no page is given. Bibliographic detail is from the Internet Archive's catalogue record of the McGraw-Hill printing, not from the item.
